paragraphs.text: This Sabbatical year signified the year of grace, the kingdom of Christ, wherein all Israelites indeed are discharged of their debts. {Mat 6:12} {See Trapp on "Mat 6:12"}

For that seventh year at least, because there was neither sowing nor reaping that year; how then could the poor pay their debts? We must all "put on bowels of mercy, forbearing one another, and forgiving one another," &c. {Col 3:12-13}
To show that none that are alienated from the life of God, or a godly life, have remission of sin by Christ: "he sanctifies all whom he justifies." Compare Rom 11:26 Isa 59:20.

Here, as in sundry other places of the new translation, the margin is better than the text, as giving a good reason of the former law, To the end that there be no poor amongst you, that is, extreme poor by your exactions. Of a cruel creditor it is said, {Psa 10:9} that "he lieth in wait to catch the poor; he doth catch the poor when he draws him into his net," that is, into bonds, debts, mortgages, as Chrysostom expounds it.
paragraphs.anchor: Save when there shall be no poor.

paragraphs.text: But "draw out thy soul to the hungry." {Isa 58:10} Many have iron bowels and withered hands. See my "Commonplace of Alms."
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt not harden thy heart.

paragraphs.text: Who is the poor man’s king, as James V of Scotland was termed for his charity.
paragraphs.anchor: And he cried unto the Lord.
Thine heart shall not be grieved.
The Lord thy God shall bless thee.

paragraphs.text: {See Trapp on "Mat 26:11"} Aged and impotent poor, whose misery moves compassion without an orator; called here our poor, as well as our brethren.
viz., Since he was sold unto thee.
Ut si non horreret servitudinem, horreret saltem ignominiam publicam: If we can bear reproach for Christ, it is an argument we mean to stick to him, as this bored servant to his master.
